Raviraj Sahu
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Shailendra Singh Thakur - Advocate for the applicant
 Shri Yogesh Dhande - Public Prosecutor for the State.
Shri Shailendra Kumar Patel - Advocate for the objector.

Order 
This is the first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

2. The applicant has been arrested on 18.06.2024 by Police Station Ghughri, District Mandla (M.P.)
in connection with Crime No.237 of 2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366A and 376(2)N of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 5(1)/6 and 5(j)(ii)/6 of the POCSO Act.
3. It is submitted that the applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case and has not committed any offence in any manner.
The applicant married the victim and their marriage certificate is Annexure A/3.
The statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. wherein she has accepted that she has stayed with the present applicant for almost 7-8 months.
She has developed pregnancy and after attaining the age of 18 years she has married the present applicant.
As on date she is residing with the present applicant in his house.
The applicant is the first offender.
The applicant is in custody since 18.06.2024.
He is ready to abide by all terms and conditions 2 MCRC-28754-2024 that may be imposed by this Court while considering this bail application.
On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail.

4. P er contra, learned counsel appearing for the State has vehemently opposed the contentions on the ground that the age of the victim at the time of commission of offence was 17 years and 07 months but he no document to disbelieve the fact that she has married the present applicant on 15.06.2024.
The applicant being the first offender as per the case diary record, is also not disputed by the State counsel.

sentences.text: 5. Counsel appearing for the objector submits that he has no objection if the bail is granted to the present applicant owing to the fact that they have married and victim is living in the house of the present applicant with him.
6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and without commenting upon the merits of the case, this Court deems it appropriate to allow this application.
Accordingly, the application is allowed subject to verification of the fact that the applicant is a first offender.
He is directed to be released on bail on furnishing surety bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one local surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of trial Court.

It is also directed that the applicant shall comply with the conditions as enumerated under Section 437(3) of Cr.P.C.
7.

This order shall remain effective till the end of the trial but in case of bail jump and breach of any of the pre-condition of bail, it shall become ineffective and cancelled without reference to this Bench.
8. The application is accordingly allowed.

(VISHAL MISHRA) JUDGE 3 MCRC-28754-2024 SSL Raviraj Sahu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101294332/
